items.title: 'If you buy Kyle, you get Kyle': Sandilands dispute returns to court
items.description: Kyle Sandilands and Jackie 'O' Henderson have separately launched legal proceedings following the termination of their $100 million contracts.

items.title: Live: Israel and Hezbollah exchange strikes as Trump announces ceasefire extension
items.description: Israel says it has launched strikes in southern Lebanon following earlier attacks in northern Israel from Hezbollah. It comes after Donald Trump announced the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon would be extended by three weeks. Follow live.

items.title: 'Homophobia has no place': AFL boss rejects ruling on slurs in sport
items.description: Both the AFL and the AFL Players' Association hit back at suggestions from the appeals board that slurs are commonplace among players in the sport.

items.title: 'Just do it': Why the gas tax momentum is building for Australia's good
items.description: Gas giants are breathing a sigh of relief after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ruled out a 25 per cent tax on exports in next month's budget. But for how long will the federal government resist something that one leading expert says is in our "national interest"?

items.title: Court shown Rebel Wilson text exchange about actor's bath incident
items.description: A Sydney court is shown a text message exchange between Hollywood star Rebel Wilson and a movie producer over a bathroom incident involving a young actor.

items.title: Perth woman warns about pedicure safety after severe infection
items.description: Kyla Willcox says she almost lost her toe from a potentially fatal infection after having a pedicure at a Perth nail salon.

items.title: AI traffic cameras set to deliver $440m fines windfall
items.description: The cameras have handed out around 184,000 infringements since they started issuing fines in October last year, according to the WA government.

items.title: Woman chooses to go blind in one eye after delays in care
items.description: A 47-year-old woman receiving care at a public eye clinic in South Australia says her experience has been so poor she is choosing to go blind in one eye.

items.title: What happens after you buy a house?
items.description: You've heard it all before: it's harder to buy a house. But, if you do manage to get your foot on the property ladder, things are also more difficult afterwards. The housing crisis has turned into an intergenerational wealth crisis, set to make paying your mortgage in retirement the norm. So how did we get there? And how do we fix it?

items.title: Live: Cowboys score five tries in first half to take big lead over Sharks
items.description: The NRL is in Queensland for a pair of Friday night clashes, as the Cowboys host the Sharks, followed by the Broncos and Bulldogs meeting in a heavyweight clash. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Tigers face resurgent Demons under MCG Friday night lights
items.description: Richmond and Melbourne meet on the MCG stage for their now-traditional Anzac Day Eve clash, as the Tigers look to get off the mark against a dangerous Demons side. Follow live.

items.title: 'People don't understand' how vital Walers were in WWI, horse trainer says
items.description: Every year on Anzac Day, for more than two decades, Janette Wilson saddles up her Waler horse and leads the procession for the Darwin march, representing the light horsemen and their companions who served in World War I.

items.title: Plan to end NDIS 'wild west' will flip rules on their head for providers
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler will end the practice of handwritten invoices, providers without qualifications and a "let it rip" market of profiteering operators. But the sector warns changes must be navigated carefully.

items.title: The consequences of India's push to get more women in parliament
items.description: India's government proposed a plan to get more women into parliament but it came with one major condition.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Trump's eleventh-hour announcement, a disabled bird and a speedy humanoid robot
items.description: It's Friday, and that means it's time to test your news knowledge from the past seven days. Were you paying attention this week?

items.title: Tradwives, gangsters and one very special dog: April's 10 best books
items.description: This month's top picks include new works from Steve Toltz and Colm Tóibín, a satire inspired by Yellowface and an investigation into the death of a London teen who masqueraded as the son of a Russian oligarch.

items.title: Jane Fonda was in her 40s when she changed the way we exercise
items.description: In the 1980s, the fitness industry as we know it was just getting started. One of the most important people in developing the way we exercise today was Jane Fonda, who released a best-selling aerobics video in 1982.

items.title: Pentagon awards $276m AUKUS contract funded by Australia
items.description: The US Department of Defense announces the first major submarine contract to deliver on the AUKUS security deal.

items.title: Norway and Türkiye follow Australia with youth social media bans
items.description: Several European nations seek to rein in children's use of social media after Australia introduced its ban last December.

items.title: UK's generational smoking ban applauded in Australia
items.description: Anyone born after 2008 will be banned from buying cigarettes or vapes for life in the UK when a new bill becomes law.

items.title: Bail denied for woman accused of repeatedly trying to kill ex-partner
items.description: The accused's lawyers applied for her release on bail last year on the basis that she had "dental and medical issues" that could not be managed in prison.

items.title: Man, 72, charged with decade-old murder of football great's brother
items.description: Victoria Police charge a Colac man with murder as part of its investigation into the 2012 suspicious disappearance of St Kilda football champion Barry Breen's brother, Brendan Breen.

items.title: Oyster growers enduring 'death by a thousand cuts' after being closed again
items.description: Oyster growing areas on the Yorke Peninsula are ordered to close due to the detection of a toxic phytoplankton for the second time this year.

items.title: Ben Roberts-Smith confirms Anzac Day plans
items.description: Ben Roberts-Smith confirms he will be attending Anzac Day services tomorrow, saying he intends to pay his respects, one week on from his release on bail.

items.title: Petrol stations fined for mismatched pricing, misleading consumers
items.description: NSW Fair Trading issues more than 200 fines to petrol stations found to have breached pricing rules. Meanwhile, motorists celebrate a drop in prices as the premier weighs future fuel security measures.
